rv.q: This is reflected in the whip-sharp book and lyrics, in which Brittain and Floyd also give us an affectionately wry snapshot of the clamour of internet-era fandom. Beneath the stupidly catchy songs, which move effortlessly through differing genres, this is a story about two people navigating a friendship through change.
Barbé and Hinds are a strong double act with yin-yang energy and impressive vocal ranges.

It arrives in the West End expanded from its original shorter format and has perhaps lost some of its charm in the process. It’s over-amplified — to the point where lyrics become inaudible — and somewhat oversold. It feels as though it’s pushing too hard when it doesn’t need to; the most effective scenes are often the quietest.
But in the more rarefied atmosphere of the West End the constant barrage of gurning and caterwauling is a major turn-off.

The show is buoyantly funny, teeming with macabre gags and Victoria Wood-esque specific one-liners, the pop-infused songs are instantly catchy (I keep humming “We’re Gonna Wow Felicia Taylor”), and there are narrative twists a-plenty.
The comedic show is a certified homicidal hoot
Bronté Barbé and Rebekah Hinds as Kathy and Stella respectively have terrific chemistry; their little jokes, cultural references and mannerisms are those of a long term friendship.
